title: Imaging the Neurologic Dog: Part 1: Considerations for Radiography.
source: PubMed · Vet Clin North Am Small Anim Pract
summary: Imaging is an important component of the clinical evaluation of neurologic patients, with radiography, computed tomography (CT), and MRI most commonly used. There are unique advantages, drawbacks, and clinical indications for each of these imaging modalities. While radiography is readily available in most practices and can diagnose many clinically relevant conditions, cross-sectional imaging (CT and MRI) is more adept at characterizing the location and extent of disease and identifying subtle disease conditions, especially primary disease of the central nervous system and peripheral nervous system. This article discusses the role of radiography in the evaluation of neurologic patients.

summary: Learning is associated with rapid microstructural changes in the human brain, yet the precise temporal dynamics of these changes remain unclear. Using dense temporal sampling of diffusion-weighted MRI (DW-MRI) combined with task-based fMRI, we assessed microstructural changes throughout a declarative learning paradigm and subsequent rest. Seventy-four participants (36 females) learned image-location associations across four encoding-retrieval repetitions while undergoing interleaved functional and DW-MRI acquisitions. summary: Venous outflow (VO) imaging describes the egress limb of the cerebral collateral circulation and has been associated with outcome in acute ischemic stroke; its added value beyond arterial collaterals and perfusion measures remains uncertain. More than a dozen VO measures have been proposed on CT and MR techniques used in acute stroke, spanning three physical signals: venous opacification, venous transit and venous oxygenation. title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
summary: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. summary: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare autoimmune astrocytopathy primarily affecting the optic nerves and spinal cord. Rapidly progressive dementia (RPD) as the initial and primary manifestation of NMOSD is exceedingly rare. summary: Peripatellar pain is usually attributed to local knee disorders. However, proximal neural lesions can also cause pain around the knee. summary: Alexithymia is the inability to identify and describe emotions, associated with an increased risk of somatic and psychiatric disease. title: Short-Video Experience and Brain-State Dynamics During the Processing of Rapidly Changing Video Information in Youth.

summary: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). summary: Psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia have been associated with older-appearing brain structure, commonly quantified using the brain-age paradigm. In this study, 61 (28 females and 33 males) antipsychotic-naïve people with first-episode psychosis were randomized to receive either a second-generation antipsychotic (risperidone or paliperidone) or placebo over a 6-month treatment period, alongside intensive psychosocial therapy. title: Disrupted cortical signatures of response inhibition in Parkinson's disease revealed by TMS-EEG.
summary: Inhibitory control deficits are a hallmark of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in patients with L-DOPA-induced dyskinesias (LID), but the cortical mechanisms underlying impaired inhibition remain poorly understood. summary: The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study provides an unprecedented opportunity to characterize adolescent brain maturation and its correlates. title: Structural food access inequalities and aging transitions: A geospatial, multistate and longitudinal analysis of UK Biobank.
summary: The food environment may influence neurodegeneration and mortality. This study examined associations of food deserts (FD) with brain health and survival using UK Biobank data. title: Structured feature disentanglement for high-fidelity unified brain MRI synthesis.
summary: Multisequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides a more reliable diagnosis in clinical applications through complementary information across sequences. However, in practice, the absence of certain MR sequences is a common problem that can lead to inconsistent analysis results. In this work, we propose a novel unified framework for synthesizing multisequence MR images, called hybrid-fusion GAN (HF-GAN). summary: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) is commonly tested when neurosarcoidosis is suspected. However, diagnostic utility is debatable. title: Optimizing myelin water imaging in multiple sclerosis.
summary: Myelin water imaging (MWI) allows in vivo quantification of myelin content using MRI. Multi-echo gradient-echo (MEGRE) sequences with Variable Flip Angles (VFA), combined with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), can generate robust, whole-brain myelin water fraction (MWF) maps more efficiently than conventional implementations. title: Diagnostic accuracy of Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI for Parkinson Disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
summary: Objective: The diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains challenging due to clinical overlap with other parkinsonian syndromes and the absence of widely available imaging biomarkers. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) enables in vivo visualization of neuromelanin in the substantia nigra (SN) and locus coeruleus (LC), where signal loss reflects dopaminergic neurodegeneration in the SN and noradrenergic neurodegeneration in the LC. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of NM-MRI in differentiating PD from healthy controls. title: Real-world efficacy and safety profile of sulthiame treatment in drug-resistant childhood epilepsy.
summary: Sulthiame (STM) is a potent carbonic anhydrase inhibitor primarily used in focal epilepsy syndromes; however, clinical data regarding its efficacy and safety in broader drug-resistant childhood epilepsy remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy, electroencephalographic response, and safety profile of STM in a cohort of pediatric patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. A retrospective medical chart review was conducted for patients under 18 years of age treated with STM at a tertiary pediatric neurology clinic between 2011 and 2024. Data including demographic characteristics, etiology, seizure semiology, epilepsy syndromes, treatment duration, and dosage were analyzed.

summary: To assess the safety, feasibility, and preliminary clinical outcomes of magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). title: Disentangling homogeneous and heterogeneous representation of human functional connectome via graph learning.
summary: Functional connectivity analysis of fMRI data provides critical insight into large-scale brain organization; however, conventional approaches often ignore the specific information mixed with population-level structure and individual- or condition-specific variability. We aimed to develop an interpretable framework that separates these shared and heterogeneous components of the human functional connectome. Approach. summary: Clinical diagnosis of tic disorders (TDs) is often delayed by fluctuating symptoms and the subjective nature of assessments. While automated methods have been proposed to bridge this gap, traditional machine learning models frequently lack robustness in unconstrained environments and fail to capture the complex, multisite tics characteristic of severe TDs. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a fine-tuned large vision-language model framework for the automated, interpretable detection of pediatric motor tics, addressing the clinical need for objective and efficient symptom assessment in unconstrained environments. summary: Young-onset Parkinson's disease (YOPD) is characterized by the onset of parkinsonism before 50 years of age and has a strong genetic contribution. We describe four patients with YOPD who were found to carry heterozygous VPS13C. In these patients, onset ranged from 37 to 45 years of age. summary: Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. title: CD8+ T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria.
summary: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. Here, we show that CD8+ T cells induce receptor-interacting serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-regulated cell death of brain endothelial cells in mouse CM, while RIPK1 phosphorylation is increased in brain endothelial cells in human CM. title: Electroencephalography-based machine learning models for hyperacute detection of large vessel occlusion stroke.
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) has shown potential as a prehospital triage instrument for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO-a) stroke. In this study, we determined the diagnostic accuracy of EEG-based machine learning algorithms for LVO-a stroke detection. Anterior circulation large vessel occlusion stroke detection machine learning models were developed using EEG data from the ELECTRA-STROKE (NCT03699397) and AI-STROKE (NCT05437237) studies. Single 2- to 3-min EEG recordings were obtained using 8 dry electrodes in adults with suspected stroke in prehospital and in-hospital settings. title: Neuromodulatory effects of audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training on subjective tinnitus, a HD-EEG study protocol.
summary: Tinnitus affects 14% of the global population, with 2% experiencing a severe form of the condition. Sound therapy using white noise emitted by hearing aids is a common intervention, supported by the phenomenon of residual inhibition observed during tinnitus assessment. This study aims to investigate whether audio-proprio-phonatory reinforcement training can improve the quality of life of patients with chronic subjective tinnitus by enabling them to listen to their own phonation, which may mask the tinnitus or induce residual inhibition. title: Cognitive correlates of diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space index in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a preliminary study.
summary: The diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index is an imaging-derived metric related to perivascular water diffusion and has been reported to correlate with global cognitive performance in dementia. However, its associations with specific cognitive functions in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) remain underexplored. This study aimed to characterize the cognitive correlates of the DTI-ALPS index in individuals with amnestic MCI. In this cross-sectional study, 57 participants with amnestic MCI underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging and a neuropsychological assessment battery. title: Repeated Exposure to Military Low-Level Blast Is Associated With Regionally Specific Reductions in Gray Matter Volume in Breachers and Snipers.
summary: To examine the association between duration of repeated exposure to low-level blast and alteration in brain structure. Data were collected at 2 neuroimaging facilities. MRI and neurocognitive data from breachers and snipers were collected prospectively at baseline (time 1) and after a training exercise involving a concentrated regimen of blast exposure (time 2) (time gap = 80.56 days, SD = 36.90). summary: Olfaction is fundamental to perception, memory, and emotion, yet the neural basis of human odor processing remains poorly understood. title: Oxygen-enhanced brain MRI using dynamic gradient-echo and MR fingerprinting.
summary: Oxygen-enhanced brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using dynamic three-dimensional (3D) gradient-echo and MR fingerprinting (MRF) was applied to evaluate oxygen transit from blood to cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). title: Hypoxia-powered MRI guides supramaximal biosurgical sampling of glioblastoma infiltration: the GLIOXY initiative.
summary: To assess the feasibility of using hypoxia-powered magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to guide prospective sampling of high-response habitats beyond contrast enhancement in glioblastoma. Nine treatment-naive patients with histologically confirmed isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype glioblastoma underwent blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) MRI during a controlled transient hypoxic stimulus on the evening before surgery. title: Resting state functional connectivity associated with maternal anxiety: preliminary evidence that infant rsFC moderates the association between behavioral inhibition and anxiety/depression.
summary: Postnatal maternal anxiety shapes caregiver and infant behavior. Yet, the relationship with infant brain function remains unclear. We examine the relation of maternal anxiety with infant resting state functional connectivity (rsFC). To evaluate the clinical significance of the rsFC networks identified, exploratory analyses tested whether the rsFC associated with maternal anxiety moderates risk trajectories from infant behavioral inhibition (BI) to childhood anxiety/depression symptoms. Four-month-old infants (N = 60) underwent resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and mothers completed the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI). title: Neural correlates underlying motor sequence task performance: handedness and sequence complexity.
summary: We aimed to determine the neural correlates of motor sequence performance in healthy young adults, with respect to handedness and sequence complexity. Strongly left-handed (LH, n = 15, 24.9y) and right-handed (RH, n = 15, 26.4y) participants performed finger key presses on a numeric keypad at four levels of sequence complexity with each hand in a randomized order. Both LH and RH performed the motor sequence task with faster reaction and motor execution times when using their right hand, irrespective of sequence complexity. title: 18F-mFBG PET Detects Neuroblastoma Recurrence Prior to 123I-mIBG SPECT.
summary: A high-risk stage M neuroblastoma patient suspected of residual disease in a T3-4 paraspinal soft tissue mass had no evidence of disease on MRI or 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT. 18F-mFBG PET/CT performed in a clinical trial showed abnormalities in the upper and lower thoracic spine, lumbar spine, and pelvis. Two months later, the MRI was unchanged, and 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT showed only an equivocal upper thoracic spine focus. 123I-mIBG SPECT/CT and MRI at 4 months post-18F-mFBG showed positive findings in the thoracic spine consistent with neuroblastoma. Follow-up confirmed that 18F-mFBG PET/CT identified neuroblastoma at least 2 months prior to 123I-mIBG and MRI.

title: Inadvertent intraspinal deployment of an iliac venous stent: a case report of surgical removal and one-year follow-up.
summary: Iliac venous stenting is an established treatment for symptomatic iliac venous obstruction and post-thrombotic disease. Although usually safe, malposition of a venous stent into the spinal canal is exceptionally rare and may cause serious neurological injury. A 53 years old woman with chronic left lower-limb swelling and pain caused by iliac venous thrombosis underwent left lower-limb venography, iliac vein balloon dilation, and stent implantation. During deployment she reported left lower-limb pain, which was initially considered procedure-related. title: Feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGANs for fracture stage determination in osteoporotic compression fractures.
summary: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a reliable indicator of fracture stage. However, MRI scans can be expensive, time-consuming, and not readily accessible to all patients. With recent advances in artificial intelligence, translating lumbar CT images into MRI images has become feasible using cycle generative adversarial network (CycleGANs) based approaches. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a model that translates lumbar CT images into MRI images (T1-weighted contrast-enhanced sequences) to predict the stage of osteoporotic compression fracture (OCFs) using conditional CycleGANs. title: Developmental trajectories of pain empathy: evidence from drift diffusion modeling and EEG time-frequency analysis.
summary: Pain empathy develops from childhood into adulthood, but the cognitive and neural processes that support this development remain incompletely understood. title: Brainstem functional connectivity integrates microbiome-gut-brain signals in healthy older adults: a cross-sectional evaluation and a randomised controlled probiotic trial
summary: Background: Despite increasing interest in the gut-brain axis, the role of the autonomic nervous system and the brainstem in human gut-brain signalling remain largely unknown. Objective: To characterise resting state functional connectivity (FC) of the brainstem in healthy older adults and to examine its association with a variety of factors relevant to ageing and the gut-brain axis, and to assess if brainstem FC is altered by probiotic intervention. title: Disability-relevant demyelination in multiple sclerosis: five-year evolution following diagnosis
summary: Improved understanding of how myelin damage contributes to disability in multiple sclerosis (MS) is needed to inform targeted therapeutic strategies and improve clinical trial platforms.
